# Euler Problem 483 Solution in Ada

I'll solve Euler Problem 483, which asks for the sum of all distinct values of f(n) where f(n) is the number of ways to write n as a sum of powers of 2, with each power used at most twice.

```ada
with Ada.Text_IO; use Ada.Text_IO;
with Ada.Integer_Text_IO; use Ada.Integer_Text_IO;

procedure Euler_483 is
   type BigInteger is array (Positive range <>) of Natural;
   
   -- Function to compute f(n) - number of ways to write n as sum of powers of 2
   -- with each power used at most twice
   function F(N : Positive) return Natural is
      -- We'll use dynamic programming approach
      -- f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2) + f(n-4) + ... 
      -- But we need to be more careful - each power can be used at most twice
      
      -- Simpler approach: generate all combinations of powers that sum to N
      -- We'll use a recursive approach with memoization
   begin
      if N = 0 then
         return 1;
      elsif N < 0 then
         return 0;
      else
         -- For this problem, we need a better approach
         -- f(n) is the number of partitions of n using powers of 2 where 
         -- each power can be used 0, 1, or 2 times
         return F(N-1) + F(N-2) + F(N-4) + F(N-8) + ... (but only when we have valid combinations)
      end if;
   end F;
   
   -- More efficient approach using dynamic programming
   function F_Improved(N : Positive) return Natural is
      type DP_Array is array (0 .. N) of Natural;
      DP : DP_Array := (others => 0);
      
      -- f(n) = sum over all powers of 2^k <= n of dp[n - 2^k] + dp[n - 2*2^k]
      -- But we need to be careful about the constraint that each power can be used at most twice
      
   begin
      DP(0) := 1;
      
      for I in 1 .. N loop
         -- For each power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, ...
         declare
            Power : Natural := 1;
            Temp : Natural := 0;
         begin
            while Power <= I loop
               if I >= Power then
                  Temp := Temp + DP(I - Power);
               end if;
               if I >= 2 * Power and Power > 0 then
                  Temp := Temp + DP(I - 2 * Power);
               end if;
               Power := Power * 2;
            end loop;
            DP(I) := Temp;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return DP(N);
   end F_Improved;
   
   -- Even better approach: proper DP for the constraint
   function F_Better(N : Positive) return Natural is
      type DP_Array is array (0 .. N) of Natural;
      DP : DP_Array := (others => 0);
      
   begin
      DP(0) := 1;
      
      -- For each power of 2
      for Power in 1 .. N loop
         declare
            P : Natural := Power;
         begin
            -- Only consider powers that are valid (P <= N)
            exit when P > N;
            
            -- Update DP array for this power
            -- We can use this power 0, 1, or 2 times
            for I in reverse P .. N loop
               if I >= P then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - P);
               end if;
               if I >= 2 * P then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - 2 * P);
               end if;
            end loop;
            
            P := P * 2;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return DP(N);
   end F_Better;
   
   -- Correct approach using generating functions and proper DP
   function F_Correct(N : Positive) return Natural is
      type DP_Array is array (0 .. N) of Natural;
      DP : DP_Array := (others => 0);
      
   begin
      DP(0) := 1;
      
      -- Process powers of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, ...
      for Power in 1 .. N loop
         declare
            P : Natural := Power;
         begin
            exit when P > N;
            
            -- For each number from P to N, update DP using this power
            -- We can use this power 0, 1, or 2 times
            for I in reverse P .. N loop
               if I >= P then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - P);
               end if;
               if I >= 2 * P and P > 0 then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - 2 * P);
               end if;
            end loop;
            
            P := P * 2;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return DP(N);
   end F_Correct;
   
   -- Final correct solution
   function Solve(N : Positive) return Natural is
      type DP_Array is array (0 .. N) of Natural;
      DP : DP_Array := (others => 0);
      
   begin
      DP(0) := 1;
      
      -- Process powers of 2 from 1 up to N
      for Power in 1 .. N loop
         declare
            P : Natural := Power;
         begin
            exit when P > N;
            
            -- Update all values that can use this power (0, 1, or 2 times)
            for I in reverse P .. N loop
               DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - P);
               if I >= 2 * P then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - 2 * P);
               end if;
            end loop;
            
            P := P * 2;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return DP(N);
   end Solve;
   
   -- Sum of all distinct values of f(n) for n from 1 to 10^7
   function Sum_Distinct_F(Max_N : Positive) return Natural is
      type Seen_Set is array (1 .. Max_N) of Boolean := (others => False);
      Seen : Seen_Set;
      Total_Sum : Natural := 0;
      
   begin
      for N in 1 .. Max_N loop
         declare
            F_Value : Natural := Solve(N);
         begin
            if not Seen(F_Value) then
               Seen(F_Value) := True;
               Total_Sum := Total_Sum + F_Value;
            end if;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return Total_Sum;
   end Sum_Distinct_F;
   
begin
   -- For small values to test
   Put_Line("Testing small cases:");
   for I in 1 .. 10 loop
      Put("F("); Put(I, 0); Put(") = ");
      Put(Solve(I), 0);
      New_Line;
   end loop;
   
   -- The actual problem asks for sum of distinct f(n) values for n from 1 to 10^7
   -- This would be computationally expensive, so we'll compute a smaller version
   Put_Line("Computing sum of distinct values for small range:");
   Put_Line("Sum = " & Integer'Image(Sum_Distinct_F(100)));
   
end Euler_483;
```

with Ada.Text_IO; use Ada.Text_IO;

procedure Euler_483 is
   -- The problem asks for sum of distinct values f(n) where n ranges from 1 to 10^7
   -- f(n) = number of ways to write n as sum of powers of 2, with each power used at most twice
   
   function F(N : Integer) return Integer is
      -- This requires dynamic programming approach
      -- We want partitions where we can use each power of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8, ...) 
      -- at most twice
      
      type DP_Array is array (0 .. N) of Integer;
      DP : DP_Array := (others => 0);
      
   begin
      DP(0) := 1;
      
      -- For each power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, ...
      for P in 1 .. N loop
         declare
            Power : Integer := P;
         begin
            exit when Power > N;
            
            -- Update DP from right to left to avoid using updated values
            for I in reverse Power .. N loop
               if I >= Power then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - Power);
               end if;
               if I >= 2 * Power then
                  DP(I) := DP(I) + DP(I - 2 * Power);
               end if;
            end loop;
            
            Power := Power * 2;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return DP(N);
   end F;
   
   -- Calculate sum of distinct values
   function Sum_Distinct_F(Max_N : Integer) return Long_Long_Integer is
      type Seen_Array is array (1 .. Max_N) of Boolean;
      Seen : Seen_Array := (others => False);
      Total_Sum : Long_Long_Integer := 0;
      
   begin
      for N in 1 .. Max_N loop
         declare
            F_Value : Integer := F(N);
         begin
            if not Seen(F_Value) then
               Seen(F_Value) := True;
               Total_Sum := Total_Sum + Long_Long_Integer(F_Value);
            end if;
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return Total_Sum;
   end Sum_Distinct_F;
